_note: Science and discoveries pilot (Kevin, 2026-11-23/24): 25 new events and 1 recategorised, plus 8 gap events (Africa, the Americas, Southeast Asia, Oceania; second batch, 2026-11-24), from Workbench "2026-11-24 Timelines science and discoveries pilot plan". Every date and place is a quoted sentence from the Wikipedia dump (checked by science.py --check). `source`: the date quote; `more`: other quoted facts (the place of work, a caveat); `claims`: other dates, ranges included. kind: the `science` sub-kind (discovery, invention, work); the generators' categories.json hold it. `tracks`: the row, where the timeline has it.

events.title: The Rhind Mathematical Papyrus is written
events.descr: An Egyptian scribe copies out the mathematical problems and tables of the Rhind papyrus, one of the two best-known mathematical papyri of ancient Egypt.

source.quote: having been written in the Fifteenth Dynasty during the late Second Intermediate Period

claims.note: A copy: the papyrus is dated c. 1550 BC by its infobox; the text it copies is older.

events.title: Babylonian astronomers begin the astronomical diaries
events.descr: Babylonian scribes begin keeping systematic day-by-day records of the sky and omens, the astronomical diaries, in the reign of Nabonassar.

source.quote: The systematic records of ominous phenomena in astronomical diaries began during the reign of Nabonassar (747–734 BC)

more.quote: The surviving tablets range in date from the mid-7th to the 1st century BC

events.title: Euclid writes the Elements
events.descr: Euclid, working in Alexandria, writes the Elements, the treatise that set out the foundations of geometry.

source.quote: It is now generally accepted that he spent his career in Alexandria and lived around 300 BC

more.quote: he is chiefly known for the Elements treatise, which established the foundations of geometry

events.title: Ptolemy completes the Almagest
events.descr: Ptolemy sets out his mathematical model of the heavens in the Almagest, which became the standard astronomical text for centuries.

source.quote: pub_date =c. 150

more.quote: Ptolemy says that the ecliptic longitudes are for the beginning of the reign of Antoninus Pius (138 AD)

events.title: Brahmagupta composes the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta
events.descr: Brahmagupta composes the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta, a treatise on astronomy and mathematics that includes rules for working with zero.

source.quote: In the year 628, at the age of 30, he composed the Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta

more.quote: Born in Bhillamāla in Gurjaradesa (modern Bhinmal in Rajasthan, India)

events.title: Zhang Heng presents his seismoscope
events.descr: Zhang Heng presents an instrument to the Han court that was said to show the direction of a distant earthquake.

source.quote: In 132, Zhang introduced an intricate seismoscope to the court

events.title: The earliest known Long Count date is carved at Chiapa de Corzo
events.descr: A stela at Chiapa de Corzo carries the earliest known contemporaneous Long Count date, the Mesoamerican system for counting days.

source.quote: The earliest contemporaneous Long Count inscription yet discovered is on Stela 2 at Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas, Mexico, showing a date of 36 BCE

claims.quote: giving the range of possible dates to fall between 236 and 19 BCE
claims.note: Takalik Abaj Stela 2, whose Long Count is battered: a range, and it might be earlier than Chiapa de Corzo.

events.title: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art reaches its final form
events.descr: A Chinese book of mathematical problems, built up by several generations of scholars, takes its received form.

source.article: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art
source.quote: composed by several generations of scholars from the 10th–2nd century BCE, its latest stage being from the 1st century CE

claims.article: The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art
claims.quote: its latest stage being from the 1st century CE
claims.note: The received text; earlier stages go back to the 10th–2nd century BCE.

events.title: Al-Khwarizmi writes the Al-Jabr, the book that names algebra
events.descr: Al-Khwarizmi writes in Baghdad a treatise on solving equations by restoration and balancing; its title gave algebra its name.

source.quote: an Arabic-language mathematical treatise on algebra written in Baghdad around 820 by Al-Khwarizmi

events.title: Ibn al-Haytham writes the Book of Optics
events.descr: Ibn al-Haytham writes his seven-volume Book of Optics in Cairo, arguing from experiment that vision comes from light entering the eye.

source.quote: written during 1011–1021

more.quote: he spent most of his productive period in the Fatimid capital of Cairo

events.title: Ulugh Beg publishes the Zīj-i Sulṭānī
events.descr: Astronomers working for Ulugh Beg at the Samarkand observatory publish a star catalogue and tables of the heavens.

source.quote: published by Ulugh Beg in 1438–1439

more.quote: working under the patronage of Ulugh Beg at Samarkand's Ulugh Beg Observatory

events.title: Madhava of Sangamagrama founds the Kerala school of mathematics
events.descr: Madhava of Sangamagrama founds the Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics, which flourished for about two centuries.

source.quote: founded the Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics

claims.article: Kerala school of astronomy and mathematics
claims.quote: The school flourished between the 14th and 16th centuries
claims.note: Madhava c. 1340 – c. 1425; the school flourished from the 14th century.

events.title: Bi Sheng invents movable type
events.descr: Bi Sheng, an artisan under the Song, makes the first movable type, one fired clay tile for each Chinese character.

source.quote: invented between 1039 and 1048

events.title: The Dresden Codex is written
events.descr: A Maya book of astronomical tables is written in the region of Chichén Itzá.

source.quote: a Maya book originating from the region of Chichén Itzá in Mexico

events.title: Gutenberg's printing press is in operation
events.descr: Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith of Mainz, gets his movable-type printing press working.

source.quote: By 1450, the press was in operation

claims.quote: It was in Strasbourg in 1440 that he is said to have perfected and unveiled the secret of printing
claims.note: The earlier date: Gutenberg is said to have perfected the technique in Strasbourg.

events.title: Ibn Khaldun writes the Muqaddimah
events.descr: Ibn Khaldun writes the Muqaddimah, an introduction to history that sets out a new science of human society.

source.quote: Book by Ibn Khaldun, written in 1377

more.quote: around which he had maintained secrecy up until his retirement to Qalʿat ibn Salama

events.title: Copernicus's De revolutionibus is printed
events.descr: Copernicus's book proposing that the Earth moves around the Sun is printed in Nuremberg.

source.quote: first printed in 1543 CE in Nuremberg, Holy Roman Empire

more.quote: born on 19 February 1473 in the city of Thorn (Toruń), in the province of Royal Prussia, in the Crown of the Kingdom of Poland

events.title: Newton publishes the Principia
events.descr: Isaac Newton publishes the Principia, which sets out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

source.quote: first published in 1687

events.title: C. V. Raman discovers Raman scattering
events.descr: C. V. Raman and his student find that light passing through a transparent material changes wavelength; he won the Nobel Prize in Physics for it in 1930.

source.quote: Raman, who discovered it in 1928

more.quote: the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS), the first research institute in India

events.title: Bose derives the quantum statistics later named for him and Einstein
events.descr: Satyendra Nath Bose derives Planck's radiation law by a new way of counting identical particles, the start of Bose–Einstein statistics.

source.quote: In 1924, whilst a Reader in the Physics Department of the University of Dhaka, Bose wrote a paper deriving Planck's quantum radiation law

events.title: Kaitai Shinsho, the Japanese anatomy book, is published
events.descr: Sugita Genpaku's Kaitai Shinsho, a translation of a Dutch anatomy text, is published and starts Japan's Dutch medical learning.

source.quote: in 1774, the third year of An'ei

events.title: Tu Youyou discovers artemisinin
events.descr: Tu Youyou finds artemisinin, a malaria drug, for which she shared the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

source.quote: It was discovered in 1972 by Tu Youyou

events.title: The first human heart transplant is performed in Cape Town
events.descr: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human-to-human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.

source.quote: Louis Washkansky received this transplant on December 3, 1967, at the Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa

events.title: The Wright brothers make the first powered, controlled flight
events.descr: Orville and Wilbur Wright make the first controlled, sustained flight of an engine-powered aircraft near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina.

source.quote: the first controlled, sustained flight of an engine-powered, heavier-than-air aircraft with the Wright Flyer on December 17, 1903

events.title: A CSIRO team builds a wireless LAN prototype
events.descr: Researchers at the CSIRO in Australia build a prototype wireless local area network; Australia, the United States and the Netherlands each claim the invention of Wi-Fi.

source.quote: A prototype test bed for a wireless local area network (WLAN) was developed in 1992 by a team of researchers from the Radiophysics Division of the CSIRO

more.quote: Australia, the United States and the Netherlands simultaneously claim the invention of Wi-Fi, and a consensus has not been reached globally

events.title: M-Pesa launches mobile money in Kenya
events.descr: Vodafone and Safaricom launch M-Pesa, a mobile-phone-based money transfer, payments and micro-financing service, in Kenya.

source.quote: launched in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom

more.quote: the largest mobile network operator in Kenya

events.title: Santos-Dumont's 14-bis makes the first publicly witnessed powered flight
events.descr: The Brazilian aeronaut Alberto Santos-Dumont flies the 14-bis near Paris, a manned powered flight witnessed by a crowd and filmed.

source.quote: In 1906, near Paris, the 14-bis made a manned powered flight that was the first to be publicly witnessed by a crowd and also filmed

events.title: Hōkūleʻa sails from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti by traditional navigation alone
events.descr: The Polynesian Voyaging Society's double-hulled voyaging canoe Hōkūleʻa completes the voyage from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti with exclusively traditional navigation techniques.

source.quote: 1976 Hawaiʻi to Tahiti voyage completed with exclusively traditional navigation techniques

events.title: David Warren builds the ARL Flight Memory Unit, a flight data recorder prototype
events.descr: The Australian scientist David Warren builds a prototype flight data recorder, the ARL Flight Memory Unit. An earlier flight data recorder, Mata-Hari, had been made in Finland in 1942.

source.quote: Warren built a prototype FDR called "The ARL Flight Memory Unit" in 1956

more.quote: was an Australian scientist, best known for inventing and developing the flight data recorder
The first modern flight data recorder, called "Mata-Hari", named after the famous spy, was created in 1942 by Finnish aviation engineer Veijo Hietala

events.title: Iron metallurgy begins in West and Central Africa
events.descr: Iron metallurgy begins in Western and Central Africa, from 2500 to 1000 BC by the article's range, with radiocarbon dates from Nigeria and the Central African Republic as early as the third millennium BC.

source.quote: the beginning of iron metallurgy in Western and Central Africa by 2500 BC - 1000 BC

claims.quote: radiocarbon and thermoluminescence dating of artifacts associated with iron metallurgy in Nigeria and the Central African Republic have yielded dates as early as the third millennium BC
claims.note: The third millennium BC (3000–2001 BC); the headline range is the article's 2500–1000 BC.

events.title: Nixtamalization: the earliest evidence, on Guatemala's southern coast
events.descr: Equipment for nixtamalization, the alkaline treatment of maize first developed in Mesoamerica, dates from 1500 to 1200 BCE on Guatemala's southern coast.

source.quote: The earliest evidence is found in Guatemala's southern coast, with equipment dating from 1200 to 1500 BCE

more.quote: The process of nixtamalization was first developed in Mesoamerica, where maize was originally cultivated

events.title: Chinampa fields, the earliest securely dated
events.descr: The earliest securely dated chinampas, the raised fields of Mesoamerican agriculture, are from the Middle Postclassic period, 1150–1350 CE.

source.quote: The earliest fields that have been securely dated are from the Middle Postclassic period, 1150–1350 CE

more.quote: is a technique used in Mesoamerican agriculture

events.title: Austronesians invent the crab claw sail
events.descr: The Austronesians invent the crab claw sail somewhere in Island Southeast Asia, by at least 2000 BCE: a latest-by date, so the sail may be older.

source.quote: The crab claw sail was invented by the Austronesians somewhere in Island Southeast Asia by at least 2000 BCE

claims.quote: They used sails some time before 2000 BCE
